items.text: A person has an experience that seems clearly to them to be a divine revelation, but nobody can independently verify it. Which assessment of factual justification is closest to your view?

options.label: The experiencer can have substantial justification from the experience alone; an outsider does not gain that much merely from the report.
Both the experiencer and an outsider hearing the report can have substantial justification without further evidence.
The experiencer may have an initial reason, but not substantial justification without further evidence.
Even the experiencer has no factual justification from the experience alone.

items.notes: The first two options explicitly affirm substantial first-person justification, while differing on outsiders' warrant. The last two deny substantial justification from the experience alone; provisional justification is not equivalent to none. The general bank source reference is not an item-validation study; the specific SEP revelation analysis is documented in the editorial review and model source audit-revelation. This item is a conceptual discriminator, not a validated independent evidence unit. Review comprehension and local dependence with EPI032 before any release.
